requirements.title: Deallocating an unallocated allocatable variable is a DEALLOCATE error condition
requirements.definition: Executing a DEALLOCATE statement for an allocatable variable that is unallocated causes an error condition in that DEALLOCATE statement. The STAT value and post-error status are owned by 9.7.4; this requirement does not invent a static diagnostic duty.

pending.unallocated-allocatable-deallocate-error: PENDING runtime source plan with an allocatable variable known unallocated immediately before DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s). The portable oracle is that s is positive and different from STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE and STAT_FAILED_IMAGE as specified by 9.7.4 p5, and that x remains unallocated as the not-successfully-deallocated object status guaranteed by 9.7.4 p6; no specific processor-dependent value is asserted and no value or bounds of x are read. This is a deterministic standard-specified error condition from 9.7.3.2 p1, not a resource failure.
pending.allocated-control-no-error: PENDING positive-control source allocating the same kind of allocatable variable before DEALLOCATE with STAT=, observing STAT=0 and then only ALLOCATED=.FALSE. by permitted inquiry plus an independent sentinel.

requirements.oracle: All facets are pending source plans. Positive plans use independent literal values, permitted allocation or pointer association inquiry results, STAT/ERRMSG observations only through their owning subclauses, finalizer call sentinels, or reached-control-flow sentinels that first establish the required preconditions. Negative plans use an otherwise conforming source and a minimal repair, with invalidity attributed to the named requirement rather than to declaration syntax, ALLOCATE ownership, NULLIFY ownership, STAT= or ERRMSG= semantics, undefined data, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted code, compiler agreement, resource exhaustion, or unsupported launch mode.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is a source-only catalogue. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no compiler, records no evidence link, approves no oracle or fixture, and claims no coverage. Future executable plans must not read deallocated allocatable storage, dereference deallocated pointer targets, read undefined pointer or C_PTR values, use address arithmetic, or rely on deliberate resource exhaustion. Multi-image execution, stopped-image handling, failed-image handling, and teams are separately gated capabilities in this suite.

requirements.title: Deallocating an allocatable TARGET makes associated pointer statuses undefined
requirements.definition: When an allocatable variable with the TARGET attribute is deallocated, the pointer association status of every pointer associated with it becomes undefined. Because undefined pointer association status is not a portable executable oracle, future tests must avoid querying or dereferencing those pointers after the deallocation.

pending.target-deallocation-undefines-associated: PENDING source-only classification plan with a pointer associated to an allocated TARGET allocatable before deallocation, recording that after DEALLOCATE the pointer association status is undefined and must not be observed by ASSOCIATED or dereferenced. A positive control may instead NULLIFY an associated pointer under 9.7.2 to demonstrate a defined disassociated status without claiming coverage of this undefined-status effect.

requirements.title: INTENT(OUT) invocation deallocates corresponding allocated allocatable actuals and subobjects
requirements.definition: On procedure invocation, any allocated allocatable object that is an actual argument corresponding to an INTENT(OUT) allocatable dummy argument is deallocated, and any allocated allocatable object that is a subobject of an actual argument corresponding to an INTENT(OUT) dummy argument is deallocated. The same deallocation-on-entry rule is stated for C invoking Fortran through a C descriptor for an allocated allocatable variable, and for Fortran invoking a C function through an interface with an INTENT(OUT) allocatable dummy before C execution begins.

pending.intent-out-actual-subobject-deallocated: PENDING complete source passing a derived-type actual with an allocated allocatable component to an INTENT(OUT) dummy, observing inside the procedure that the component is unallocated before any definition and then assigning fresh literals. pending.fortran-calls-c-actual-deallocated-befor: PENDING source plan with Fortran invoking a C function through an interface declaring an INTENT(OUT) allocatable dummy and an allocated allocatable actual; the C side observes descriptor state consistent with deallocation before C execution. requirements.title: Coarray deallocation synchronizes active images and succeeds only on all active images
requirements.definition: Executing a statement that deallocates a coarray or an object with a coarray potential subobject component includes implicit synchronization of all active images in the current team. A stopped or failed image in the current team causes an error condition. If no other error occurs, active images are delayed after the statement until all other active images in the current team have executed the same statement the same number of times in that team; segments before the statement on an active image precede segments after the statement on another active image; and a coarray shall not become deallocated on an image unless it is successfully deallocated on all active images in the team.

pending.implicit-synchronization: PENDING multi-image source requiring at least two images and separately gated multi-image execution. All active images allocate the same coarray, set independent pre-deallocation sentinels, execute the same DEALLOCATE with STAT=, and observe only post-statement sentinels and permitted ALLOCATED status after all STAT values are zero.
pending.stopped-or-failed-image-error-condition: PENDING source-only gated classification for the case where the current team already contains a stopped or failed image. Do not attempt to manufacture, force, or rely on creating a stopped or failed image; that condition is not portably producible by this suite. If a separately provisioned stopped/failed-image capability supplies the condition, the portable oracle is only the 9.7.4/16.10.2 STAT_STOPPED_IMAGE or STAT_FAILED_IMAGE result and the 9.7.4 p6 status consequences; otherwise this facet remains pending.
pending.same-statement-same-count-delay: PENDING multi-image source requiring at least two images and separately gated multi-image execution. Each active image executes the same coarray DEALLOCATE statement the same number of times in the team, with per-iteration literal counters showing the post-statement segment is reached only after matching participation.
pending.segment-ordering: PENDING multi-image source requiring at least two images and separately gated multi-image execution. pending.all-active-images-success-before-dealloc: PENDING multi-image source requiring at least two images and separately gated multi-image execution. requirements.title: Automatic deallocation has the effect of DEALLOCATE without dealloc options
requirements.definition: Automatic deallocation has the same effect as a DEALLOCATE statement without a dealloc-opt-list. STAT= and ERRMSG= are therefore not present for automatic deallocation unless another owning construct provides its own status mechanism.

pending.automatic-deallocation-same-effect: PENDING source plan comparing an automatic deallocation event, such as procedure return or END BLOCK for an unsaved allocated allocatable local, with an explicit DEALLOCATE-without-options control using finalizer counters and independent sentinels. No deallocated object is referenced after the event.
pending.automatic-deallocation-no-dealloc-option: PENDING source-only classification plan recording that automatic deallocation cannot be tested through DEALLOCATE STAT= or ERRMSG= options from 9.7.3.1. Future fixtures must use independently observable effects such as finalization counters or subsequent invocation status, and must not invent a hidden STAT variable.

requirements.oracle: All facets are pending source plans. Positive plans use independent literal values, permitted allocation or pointer association inquiry results, STAT/ERRMSG observations only through their owning subclauses, finalizer call sentinels, or reached-control-flow sentinels that first establish the required preconditions. Negative plans use an otherwise conforming source and a minimal repair, with invalidity attributed to the named requirement rather than to declaration syntax, ALLOCATE ownership, NULLIFY ownership, STAT= or ERRMSG= semantics, undefined data, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted code, compiler agreement, resource exhaustion, or unsupported launch mode.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is a source-only catalogue. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no compiler, records no evidence link, approves no oracle or fixture, and claims no coverage. Numbered syntax rules and constraints carry the processor detection/reporting duty from 4.2; unnumbered prose effects, execution-time allocation status, pointer association status, STAT values, error conditions, image participation, processor-dependent outcomes, and coarray synchronization requirements are not promoted to mandatory static diagnostics. Future executable plans must not read deallocated allocatable storage, dereference deallocated pointer targets, read undefined pointer or C_PTR values, use address arithmetic, or rely on deliberate resource exhaustion. Multi-image execution, stopped-image handling, failed-image handling, and teams are separately gated capabilities in this suite.
